case_studies.title: Leveraging LLMs for Multi-File DSL Code Generation: An Industrial Case Study
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on general-purpose code generation, yet their applicability to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) remains underexplored, especially for repository-scale change generation spanning multiple files and folder structures from a single natural-language (NL) instruction. We report an industrial case study at BMW that adapts code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL that drives downstream Java/TypeScript code generation. We develop an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction, multi-file task r
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the lack of applicability of large language models (LLMs) to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) for repository-scale change generation. The AI approach involves adapting code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL. The outcome is an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction and multi-file task generation, which has been applied in an industrial case study at BMW.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can develop an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction and multi-file task generation, leveraging code-oriented LLMs to adapt to their specific DSL and use case. By doing so, they can achieve efficient and scalable code generation and modification, streamlining their development process.
case_studies.monetisation: This study presents a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and market AI-powered code generation tools tailored to specific DSLs and industries. By commercializing this technology, companies can help enterprises improve their code development efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance overall productivity.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is hindered by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. The AI approach involves a systematic analysis of model-hardware co-characterization to evaluate model-hardware pairs under cost, energy, and time constraints. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient than desktop-grade GPUs for low-cost VLA deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can use a cross-accelerator leaderboard to evaluate model-hardware pairs and identify the most efficient combinations for their specific use case. By considering the constraints of cost, energy, and time, practitioners can optimize their VLA models for on-robot deployment.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has monetisation potential in the development of efficient and cost-effective robotic systems, which can be applied to various industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and service robots. Companies can leverage this research to create products that integrate VLA models with edge devices, enabling real-time inference and control for robots in various settings.

case_studies.title: On-Device Vision Training, Deployment, and Inference on a Thumb-Sized Microcontroller
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline, comprising data acquisition, two-layer CNN training with Adam optimization, and real-time inference, executing entirely on a microcontroller-class device costing $15-40 USD. Unlike cloud-based workflows that require external infrastructure and conceal the computational pipeline from the practitioner, this system implements every step of the core ML lifecycle in approximately 1,750 lines of readable C++ that compiles in under one minute using the Arduino IDE, with no external ML dependencies. Running on the S
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the need for a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline that can run on a low-cost microcontroller. The AI approach used is a two-layer CNN trained with Adam optimization, which enables real-time inference on the device. The outcome is a system that can execute the entire ML lifecycle on a $15-40 USD microcontroller-class device, making it a promising solution for edge AI applications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can use the Arduino IDE to develop and deploy their own on-device vision ML models, leveraging the provided C++ code as a starting point. By doing so, they can create compact, efficient, and real-time capable ML models that can run on resource-constrained devices, expanding the reach of AI to new applications and use cases.
case_studies.monetisation: The monetisation potential of this study lies in the development of low-cost, edge AI-powered devices for various industries, such as surveillance, robotics, or healthcare. Companies can build upon this research to create products that leverage the efficiency and scalability of on-device vision ML, providing a competitive edge in the market and generating revenue through device sales or subscription-based services.

case_studies.title: A Deployable Embodied Vision-Language Navigation System with Hierarchical Cognition and Context-Aware Exploration
case_studies.abstract: Bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment remains a key challenge in intelligent robotic systems, where perception, reasoning, and planning must operate under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution. In vision-language navigation (VLN), existing approaches often face a fundamental trade-off between strong reasoning capabilities and efficient deployment on real-world platforms. In this paper, we present a deployable embodied VLN system that achieves both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning on real-world robotic platform
case_studies.summary: The problem of bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment in intelligent robotic systems is addressed in this paper. The AI approach presented is a deployable embodied vision-language navigation system that achieves both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning on real-world robotic platforms. The outcome of this system is the ability to navigate and interact with environments in a more human-like way, with potential applications in various fields such as robotics and autonomous systems.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing hierarchical cognition and context-aware exploration capabilities in their own systems, allowing for more efficient and effective navigation and interaction with environments. By leveraging vision-language navigation and embodied intelligence, practitioners can create more robust and adaptable AI systems that can operate in real-world settings.
case_studies.monetisation: The presented system has concrete business opportunities in industries such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart homes, where efficient and robust navigation and interaction with environments are crucial. Companies can integrate this technology into their products and services, such as autonomous robots or virtual assistants, to enhance user experience and improve overall performance.

case_studies.title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Industrial robotic manipulation demands reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong generalization, they remain fundamentally reactive. By optimizing the next action given the current observation without evaluating potential futures, they are brittle to the compounding failure modes of long-horizon tasks. Cortex 2.0 shifts from reactive control to plan-and-act by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them for expected success and efficiency, then com
case_studies.summary: Industrial robotic manipulation tasks require reliable long-horizon execution, but current Vision-Language-Action models are reactive and prone to failure. Cortex 2.0 addresses this by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space and scoring them for expected success and efficiency. This plan-and-act approach has the potential to improve the reliability and efficiency of industrial robotic manipulation tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing models that generate and evaluate potential future trajectories, rather than just reacting to the current observation. By doing so, they can create more robust and efficient systems for long-horizon tasks.
case_studies.monetisation: The Cortex 2.0 approach has clear potential for monetization in the industrial automation sector, where reliable and efficient robotic manipulation is critical. Companies can develop and market products based on this technology, offering improved performance and reduced downtime for industrial robotic systems.

case_studies.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
case_studies.abstract: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM), maintained by the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) collaboration, enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients in 83 countries. Yet generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process requiring clinical, epidemiological and technical expertise. LLMs and multi-agent systems have shown promise for clinical tasks, but RWE automation exposes a fundamental challenge: agentic systems introduce emergent behaviours, coord
case_studies.summary: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM) has harmonised electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients, but generating real-world evidence from these repositories remains a manual process. The authors propose FastOMOP, a foundational architecture that utilizes AI agents and LLMs to automate the process of generating real-world evidence. This approach has the potential to introduce emergent behaviours and improve the efficiency of real-world evidence generation, but its practical application and outcomes are still theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners should consider the use of multi-agent systems and LLMs in automating clinical tasks, but also be aware of the potential challenges and limitations of introducing emergent behaviours. By understanding the trade-offs between automation and control, practitioners can design more effective and reliable systems for real-world evidence generation.
case_studies.monetisation: The FastOMOP architecture presents a concrete business opportunity for companies that provide healthcare data analytics and real-world evidence services, as it has the potential to reduce costs and improve efficiency. By developing and marketing a product based on this architecture, companies can capitalize on the growing demand for automated real-world evidence generation and establish themselves as leaders in the field of healthcare AI.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, LLMs, Automation, Healthcare AI

case_studies.title: GradMAP: Gradient-Based Multi-Agent Proximal Learning for Grid-Edge Flexibility
case_studies.abstract: Coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices requires learning methods that remain fully decentralised in deployment while still respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This paper proposes gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning (GradMAP) to address this challenge. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing, and each agent uses only its own local observation for online decision-making without communication. During offline training, GradMAP embeds a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model in a primal-dual le
case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices in a decentralized manner while respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics is addressed. The proposed AI approach, GradMAP, uses gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning to train independent neural-network policies for each agent. The outcome of this approach is a fully decentralized learning method that can learn to make online decisions without communication between agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the GradMAP approach to other decentralized control problems by using a differentiable model of the underlying physics and training independent neural-network policies for each agent. This approach can be particularly useful in situations where communication between agents is limited or impossible.
case_studies.monetisation: The GradMAP approach has the potential to be commercialized as a software solution for grid-edge device management, providing a decentralized and efficient way to control and optimize the behavior of these devices. This could be particularly valuable for companies that operate large numbers of grid-edge devices, such as utilities or renewable energy providers.

case_studies.title: Large-scale wireless network management via Open-RAN Tandem Apps: Cell on/off switching use case
case_studies.abstract: With growing mobile-network complexity, management and optimization have become increasingly difficult. Centralized algorithms face high control-data overhead and computational load, while distributed approaches often perform far from optimally. The O-RAN architecture introduces two tiers of RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), enabling hierarchical network-management schemes. This work proposes Tandem Apps: a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both controllers. We show how to design Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve an agile, low-comp
case_studies.summary: The increasing complexity of mobile networks poses significant management and optimization challenges, with traditional centralized and distributed approaches facing limitations. This work proposes Tandem Apps, a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs) in the O-RAN architecture, to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. The proposed approach demonstrates potential for improved network management through the cell on/off switching use case.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the concept of Tandem Apps by designing hierarchical optimization mechanisms that leverage the strengths of both centralized and distributed approaches. By splitting optimization mechanisms into tightly coupled components, practitioners can develop more agile and efficient network management solutions.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed Tandem Apps approach offers a clear opportunity for product development, particularly in the context of 5G and 6G network management, where optimized network performance is crucial. Companies can capitalize on this idea by developing and marketing Tandem Apps-based solutions for wireless network management, targeting telecommunications operators and equipment manufacturers.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Templates: A Unified Plugin Framework for Controllable Diffusion
case_studies.abstract: Controllable diffusion methods have substantially expanded the practical utility of diffusion models, but they are typically developed as isolated, backbone-specific systems with incompatible training pipelines, parameter formats, and runtime hooks. This fragmentation makes it difficult to reuse infrastructure across tasks, transfer capabilities across backbones, or compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline. We present Diffusion Templates, a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The framework is organiz
case_studies.summary: The current controllable diffusion methods are fragmented and incompatible, making it difficult to reuse infrastructure or transfer capabilities across different models. The proposed Diffusion Templates framework addresses this issue by providing a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. This framework enables the reuse of infrastructure and transfer of capabilities across different models, potentially leading to more efficient and effective controllable diffusion methods.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this framework, AI practitioners can start by identifying the specific controllable diffusion capabilities they want to inject into their base model and then use the Diffusion Templates framework to decouple and reuse these capabilities. By doing so, they can develop more flexible and efficient controllable diffusion pipelines that can be easily adapted to different tasks and models.
case_studies.monetisation: The Diffusion Templates framework has the potential to be monetized by offering it as a software development kit (SDK) or a cloud-based service that provides a unified platform for controllable diffusion capabilities. This could be particularly attractive to companies that rely on controllable diffusion methods for their AI applications, such as image and video generation, text-to-image synthesis, and data augmentation.

case_studies.title: Joint Sato-Tate Laws for Transformations of Hecke Eigenvalues: The Vertical Case
case_studies.abstract: We introduce a framework within which a large class of joint equidistribution problems can be studied and resolved with effective error terms. This involves proving a higher dimensional and $μ$-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause (H-K) variation from analysis, where, in particular, we formulate a technique to approximate a broad class of relevant functions by functions of bounded H-K variation. Our main focus will be on the vertical Sato-Tate problem for spaces of cusp forms and for families of elliptic curves over finite fields. In particular,
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues, which is a fundamental issue in number theory. The AI approach involves utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause variation and formulating a technique to approximate relevant functions. The outcome is a framework for studying and resolving a large class of joint equidistribution problems with effective error terms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can utilize the proposed framework to study joint equidistribution problems in other fields, such as cryptography and coding theory. By leveraging the techniques developed in this study, researchers can approximate complex functions and analyze their distributions, leading to new insights and discoveries.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of advanced cryptographic protocols and secure coding schemes, which can be licensed to companies operating in the fintech and cybersecurity industries. Additionally, the framework proposed in this study can be adapted to analyze and optimize complex systems, leading to potential applications in fields such as logistics and supply chain management.

case_studies.title: Learning to Think from Multiple Thinkers
case_studies.abstract: We study learning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, all of whom provide correct but possibly systematically different solutions, e.g., step-by-step solutions to math problems written by different thinkers, or step-by-step execution traces of different programs solving the same problem. We consider classes that are computationally easy to learn using CoT supervision from a single thinker, but hard to learn with only end-result supervision, i.e., without CoT (Joshi et al. 2025). We establish that, under cryptographic assumptions, learning can be hard from CoT superv
case_studies.summary: The problem of learning from multiple thinkers is studied, where each thinker provides correct but possibly systematically different solutions. The AI approach involves using Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers to learn classes that are computationally easy to learn with CoT supervision from a single thinker. The outcome establishes that learning can be hard from CoT supervision under cryptographic assumptions.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this research by considering the limitations of learning from multiple thinkers and the potential cryptographic assumptions that may affect the learning process. To overcome these challenges, practitioners can explore alternative approaches, such as using ensemble methods or transfer learning, to improve the robustness of their models.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity is to develop AI-powered educational platforms that can learn from multiple thinkers and provide personalized learning experiences for students. By leveraging the insights from this research, companies can create more effective and efficient learning systems that can adapt to different thinking styles and problem-solving approaches.

case_studies.title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed, yet their outputs can be highly sensitive to routine, non-adversarial variation in how users phrase queries, a gap not well addressed by existing red-teaming efforts. We propose Green Shielding, a user-centric agenda for building evidence-backed deployment guidance by characterizing how benign input variation shifts model behavior. We operationalize this agenda through the CUE criteria: benchmarks with authentic Context, reference standards and metrics that capture true Utility, and perturbations that reflect realistic variations in the E
case_studies.summary: The problem of large language models being sensitive to minor variations in user queries is addressed through the Green Shielding approach, which aims to characterize how benign input variation shifts model behavior. The proposed approach operationalizes the CUE criteria to provide evidence-backed deployment guidance. The outcome of this approach is expected to lead to more trustworthy AI models that can provide consistent and reliable outputs despite variations in user input.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the Green Shielding approach, AI practitioners should focus on designing benchmarks that reflect authentic user contexts and behaviors, as well as developing metrics that capture the true utility of their models. By doing so, practitioners can identify and mitigate potential issues related to input variation, leading to more robust and reliable AI systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The Green Shielding approach presents a potential business opportunity for companies that specialize in AI model development and deployment, as it can help them provide more trustworthy and reliable models to their clients. By incorporating the CUE criteria into their development workflow, companies can differentiate themselves from competitors and establish a leadership position in the AI market.

case_studies.title: Can Current Agents Close the Discovery-to-Application Gap? A Case Study in Minecraft
case_studies.abstract: Discovering causal regularities and applying them to build functional systems--the discovery-to-application loop--is a hallmark of general intelligence, yet evaluating this capacity has been hindered by the vast complexity gap between scientific discovery and real-world engineering. We introduce SciCrafter, a Minecraft-based benchmark that operationalizes this loop through parameterized redstone circuit tasks. Agents must ignite lamps in specified patterns (e.g., simultaneously or in timed sequences); scaling target parameters substantially increases construction complexity and required knowle
case_studies.summary: The discovery-to-application gap in general intelligence is a significant problem that hinders the evaluation of AI systems, and the authors propose a Minecraft-based benchmark called SciCrafter to address this issue. The AI approach uses parameterized redstone circuit tasks to operationalize the discovery-to-application loop, where agents must ignite lamps in specified patterns. The outcome of this study provides insights into the capabilities of current agents in closing the discovery-to-application gap, but its practical applications and scalability are still uncertain.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by using Minecraft-based benchmarks to evaluate the discovery-to-application capabilities of their AI systems, and by focusing on developing agents that can learn from complex environments. The use of parameterized tasks can help to increase the complexity and scalability of AI systems, making them more applicable to real-world problems.
case_studies.monetisation: The SciCrafter benchmark has potential for monetization as a tool for evaluating and improving AI systems, particularly in industries that require complex problem-solving and adaptive learning. Companies can utilize this benchmark to develop more advanced AI agents that can be applied to real-world problems, such as robotics, gaming, or smart homes, and provide a competitive edge in the market.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation
case_studies.abstract: This paper investigates whether source trustworthiness shapes Turkish evidential morphology and whether large language models (LLMs) track this sensitivity. We study the past-domain contrast between -DI and -mIs in controlled cloze contexts where the information source is overtly external, while only its perceived reliability is manipulated (High-Trust vs. Low-Trust). In a human production experiment, native speakers of Turkish show a robust trust effect: High-Trust contexts yield relatively more -DI, whereas Low-Trust contexts yield relatively more -mIs, with the pattern remaining stable acro
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating source trustworthiness in Turkish evidential morphology is addressed through a controlled experiment. The AI approach involves studying the performance of large language models (LLMs) in tracking source sensitivity. The outcome shows a robust trust effect, with native speakers and LLMs yielding different results based on High-Trust and Low-Trust contexts.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can design similar experiments to test the source sensitivity of LLMs in other languages and contexts. By doing so, they can improve the performance of LLMs in tracking evidential morphology and enhance their ability to reason about source trustworthiness.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has potential for monetisation in the development of more accurate and reliable language models, particularly in applications where trustworthiness and source evaluation are crucial, such as fact-checking and news analysis. A concrete business opportunity could be the creation of a language model-based tool for evaluating the credibility of online sources.

case_studies.title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
case_studies.abstract: As human-AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction are needed. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory. The PCS captures an agent's perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support. Both scales were adapted
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating human-AI cooperation has led to the development of two new scales, the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale, which capture the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction. The AI approach used in this study is based on joint activity theory and evolutionary cooperation theory, providing a theoretically grounded framework for assessing human-AI teamwork. The outcome of this study is the introduction of two new scales that can be used to measure the success of human-AI cooperation, providing a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the field.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research in practice, AI practitioners can use the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale to evaluate the effectiveness of their human-AI teamwork and identify areas for improvement. By using these scales, practitioners can develop more effective human-AI collaboration systems that are tailored to the needs of their users.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of a consultancy service that helps organizations evaluate and improve their human-AI teamwork using the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale. This service could provide a valuable revenue stream for companies that specialize in AI implementation and human-AI collaboration.

case_studies.summary: The problem addressed is the existence of multiple positive normalized solutions to a coupled Schrödinger system with prescribed masses. The AI approach involves mathematical modeling and analysis of the system using techniques from partial differential equations and functional analysis. The outcome is the establishment of multiple positive solutions under certain conditions, contributing to the understanding of the system's behavior.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can utilize the mathematical frameworks developed to analyze and solve similar systems, adapting the methods to their specific problems of interest. By understanding the conditions under which multiple positive solutions exist, practitioners can better design and optimize systems that rely on such phenomena.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity lies in developing software or consulting services that apply the insights from this research to real-world problems in physics, engineering, or other fields where coupled Schrödinger systems are relevant. Companies could offer tailored solutions or simulations based on the models developed from this research, targeting industries such as materials science, quantum computing, or telecommunications.

case_studies.summary: The problem of bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment in intelligent robotic systems is addressed through a vision-language navigation system. The AI approach involves hierarchical cognition and context-aware exploration to achieve both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning. The outcome is a deployable embodied vision-language navigation system that can operate on real-world robotic platforms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can focus on developing hierarchical cognitive models that balance strong reasoning capabilities with efficient deployment on real-world platforms. By integrating context-aware exploration, practitioners can improve the robustness and adaptability of their AI systems in dynamic environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The developed system has a concrete business opportunity in the robotics and autonomous systems industry, where efficient and robust navigation systems are in high demand. Companies can adapt and license this technology to enhance their robotic products, such as service robots, drones, or self-driving cars, and create new revenue streams.

case_studies.title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Industrial robotic manipulation demands reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong generalization, they remain fundamentally reactive. By optimizing the next action given the current observation without evaluating potential futures, they are brittle to the compounding failure modes of long-horizon tasks. Cortex 2.0 shifts from reactive control to plan-and-act by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them for expected success and efficiency, then com
case_studies.summary: Industrial robotic manipulation requires reliable long-horizon execution, but current Vision-Language-Action models are reactive and prone to failure. Cortex 2.0 addresses this by shifting to a plan-and-act approach, generating candidate future trajectories and scoring them for success and efficiency. This approach enables more robust and efficient execution of industrial robotic tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing models that generate and evaluate potential future trajectories, rather than just reacting to current observations. By incorporating planning and evaluation into their models, practitioners can create more robust and efficient AI systems for industrial robotic manipulation.
case_studies.monetisation: The Cortex 2.0 approach presents a clear business opportunity for companies developing industrial robotic systems, as it enables more efficient and reliable execution of tasks. By integrating this technology into their products, companies can differentiate themselves and attract customers seeking more robust and efficient industrial robotic solutions.

case_studies.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
case_studies.abstract: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM), maintained by the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) collaboration, enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients in 83 countries. Yet generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process requiring clinical, epidemiological and technical expertise. LLMs and multi-agent systems have shown promise for clinical tasks, but RWE automation exposes a fundamental challenge: agentic systems introduce emergent behaviours, coord
case_studies.summary: The generation of real-world evidence from large health record datasets is a manual process that requires significant expertise, limiting its scalability and efficiency. The proposed FastOMOP architecture utilizes AI and multi-agent systems to automate this process, leveraging the OMOP Common Data Model to harmonize data from diverse sources. By automating real-world evidence generation, FastOMOP aims to improve the speed and reliability of clinical research and decision-making.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the principles of FastOMOP, AI practitioners should focus on developing architectures that integrate multiple AI systems and data models to automate complex tasks, such as real-world evidence generation. By leveraging existing data standards like OMOP CDM, practitioners can ensure interoperability and facilitate the adoption of their solutions in real-world settings.
case_studies.monetisation: The FastOMOP architecture presents a concrete business opportunity for companies specializing in healthcare data analytics and clinical research, as it offers a scalable and efficient solution for generating real-world evidence. By commercializing FastOMOP or similar architectures, businesses can provide valuable services to pharmaceutical companies, research institutions, and healthcare providers, helping them make data-driven decisions and improve patient outcomes.
case_studies.relevance_tag: Healthcare AI, Automation, AI Agents, LLMs

case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. We introduce AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework scoring 50 agents across 10 workload categories along four factors (Benchmark Performance, Adoption Signals, Community Sentiment, and Ecosystem Health) aggregated from 18 real-time signals across GitHub, package registries, IDE marketplaces, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards. Three analyses ground the framework. The four factors capture largely complementary information (n=50; $ρ_{\
case_studies.summary: The evaluation of AI agents is limited by static benchmarks that do not account for real-world deployment and user experience. The proposed AgentPulse framework addresses this by introducing a continuous evaluation methodology that assesses AI agents across multiple factors and signals. The framework demonstrates its effectiveness through analyses of 50 agents across 10 workload categories, providing a more comprehensive understanding of AI agent performance and adoption.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this framework, AI practitioners can integrate AgentPulse into their development workflows to monitor and evaluate their AI agents' performance and adoption in real-time. By using a multi-signal approach, practitioners can identify areas for improvement and optimize their AI agents for better deployment and user experience.
case_studies.monetisation: The AgentPulse framework presents a business opportunity for companies to develop and market AI evaluation and monitoring tools that help organizations optimize their AI deployments. By providing a comprehensive and continuous evaluation methodology, companies can offer valuable insights and services to AI developers and users, generating revenue through software sales, subscriptions, or consulting services.

case_studies.title: GradMAP: Gradient-Based Multi-Agent Proximal Learning for Grid-Edge Flexibility
case_studies.abstract: Coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices requires learning methods that remain fully decentralised in deployment while still respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This paper proposes gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning (GradMAP) to address this challenge. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing, and each agent uses only its own local observation for online decision-making without communication. During offline training, GradMAP embeds a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model in a primal-dual le
case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices in a decentralised manner while respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics is addressed in this paper. The proposed AI approach, GradMAP, uses gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning to train independent neural-network policies for each agent. The outcome of this approach is a decentralised learning method that enables online decision-making without communication among agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilise the GradMAP framework to develop decentralised learning methods for other complex systems. By embedding differentiable models into a primal-dual learning framework, practitioners can enable independent agents to learn and make decisions in a decentralised manner.
case_studies.monetisation: The GradMAP approach has potential for monetisation in the energy sector, particularly in the development of smart grid technologies. Companies can utilise this approach to create products that enable decentralised coordination of grid-edge devices, leading to improved efficiency and reliability in energy distribution.

case_studies.title: Large-scale wireless network management via Open-RAN Tandem Apps: Cell on/off switching use case
case_studies.abstract: With growing mobile-network complexity, management and optimization have become increasingly difficult. Centralized algorithms face high control-data overhead and computational load, while distributed approaches often perform far from optimally. The O-RAN architecture introduces two tiers of RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), enabling hierarchical network-management schemes. This work proposes Tandem Apps: a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both controllers. We show how to design Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve an agile, low-comp
case_studies.summary: The growing complexity of mobile networks has made management and optimization increasingly difficult, with centralized algorithms facing high control-data overhead and distributed approaches often performing suboptimally. This work proposes Tandem Apps, a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs) in the O-RAN architecture, to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. The proposed approach enables hierarchical network-management schemes, but its practical implementation and outcome are still theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can explore the design of Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. By leveraging the O-RAN architecture and RICs, practitioners can develop hierarchical network-management schemes that address the limitations of centralized and distributed approaches.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed Tandem Apps concept has monetisation potential as it can be adapted to various network management scenarios, offering a clear product opportunity for companies specializing in network optimization and management solutions. By developing and refining this concept, companies can create tailored products and services that address the growing need for efficient and scalable network management solutions.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Templates: A Unified Plugin Framework for Controllable Diffusion
case_studies.abstract: Controllable diffusion methods have substantially expanded the practical utility of diffusion models, but they are typically developed as isolated, backbone-specific systems with incompatible training pipelines, parameter formats, and runtime hooks. This fragmentation makes it difficult to reuse infrastructure across tasks, transfer capabilities across backbones, or compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline. We present Diffusion Templates, a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The framework is organiz
case_studies.summary: The problem of fragmentation in controllable diffusion methods is addressed by decoupling base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The AI approach, known as Diffusion Templates, provides a unified and open plugin framework for integrating various controllable diffusion methods. This framework allows for greater flexibility and reusability of infrastructure across tasks, enabling the composition of multiple controls within a single generation pipeline.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this framework by developing plugins for specific controllable diffusion methods, allowing for seamless integration with existing base models. By doing so, they can create more flexible and reusable generation pipelines, facilitating the transfer of capabilities across different backbone models.
case_studies.monetisation: The Diffusion Templates framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing AI-powered generative models, as it enables the creation of more versatile and adaptable models. By licensing or integrating this framework, businesses can accelerate their development of controllable diffusion methods, providing a competitive edge in applications such as image and video generation, music synthesis, and text-to-speech systems.

case_studies.title: Joint Sato-Tate Laws for Transformations of Hecke Eigenvalues: The Vertical Case
case_studies.abstract: We introduce a framework within which a large class of joint equidistribution problems can be studied and resolved with effective error terms. This involves proving a higher dimensional and $μ$-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause (H-K) variation from analysis, where, in particular, we formulate a technique to approximate a broad class of relevant functions by functions of bounded H-K variation. Our main focus will be on the vertical Sato-Tate problem for spaces of cusp forms and for families of elliptic curves over finite fields. In particular,
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues for cusp forms and elliptic curves over finite fields. The AI approach involves utilizing the theory of Hardy-Krause variation and formulating a technique to approximate relevant functions. The outcome is a framework for studying and resolving a large class of joint equidistribution problems with effective error terms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the technique of approximating functions of bounded Hardy-Krause variation to other problems in number theory and analysis. This approach can be used to resolve equidistribution problems in various mathematical contexts, providing a powerful tool for analyzing complex systems.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity is to develop software that utilizes this framework to analyze and optimize mathematical models in fields such as cryptography and coding theory. Companies specializing in mathematical modeling and analysis can leverage this research to create innovative products and services.

case_studies.title: Learning to Think from Multiple Thinkers
case_studies.abstract: We study learning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, all of whom provide correct but possibly systematically different solutions, e.g., step-by-step solutions to math problems written by different thinkers, or step-by-step execution traces of different programs solving the same problem. We consider classes that are computationally easy to learn using CoT supervision from a single thinker, but hard to learn with only end-result supervision, i.e., without CoT (Joshi et al. 2025). We establish that, under cryptographic assumptions, learning can be hard from CoT superv
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the difficulty of learning from Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, which can provide correct but systematically different solutions. The AI approach involves learning with CoT supervision from multiple thinkers, analyzing the impact of cryptographic assumptions on the learning process. The outcome of this study establishes the hardness of learning from CoT supervision under certain assumptions, providing insights into the limitations of CoT learning.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners should consider the potential biases and limitations of CoT supervision from multiple thinkers when designing and training AI models. This can involve carefully evaluating the consistency and quality of the supervision data to ensure that the model learns effectively and generalizes well to new situations.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this study is the development of AI models that can effectively learn from diverse and potentially biased supervision data, which could be applied in areas such as education or decision support systems. By addressing the challenges of CoT learning from multiple thinkers, companies can create more robust and reliable AI solutions that can handle complex and nuanced tasks.

case_studies.title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed, yet their outputs can be highly sensitive to routine, non-adversarial variation in how users phrase queries, a gap not well addressed by existing red-teaming efforts. We propose Green Shielding, a user-centric agenda for building evidence-backed deployment guidance by characterizing how benign input variation shifts model behavior. We operationalize this agenda through the CUE criteria: benchmarks with authentic Context, reference standards and metrics that capture true Utility, and perturbations that reflect realistic variations in the E
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the sensitivity of large language models to variations in user input, which can lead to inconsistent and potentially misleading results. The proposed approach, Green Shielding, is a user-centric agenda that characterizes how benign input variation shifts model behavior through the CUE criteria. The outcome of this approach is the development of evidence-backed deployment guidance for building trustworthy AI models.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the lessons from this study, AI practitioners can prioritize the development of user-centric evaluation metrics that capture realistic variations in user input, rather than relying on traditional red-teaming efforts. By doing so, they can create more robust and trustworthy AI models that are better equipped to handle the complexities of real-world user interactions.
case_studies.monetisation: The Green Shielding approach has the potential to be monetized as a consulting service or software product that helps organizations develop and deploy more trustworthy AI models, particularly in industries where reliability and consistency are critical, such as healthcare or finance. Companies that develop and market AI-powered products could benefit from integrating the CUE criteria into their development and testing processes to differentiate themselves from competitors and build trust with their customers.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation
case_studies.abstract: This paper investigates whether source trustworthiness shapes Turkish evidential morphology and whether large language models (LLMs) track this sensitivity. We study the past-domain contrast between -DI and -mIs in controlled cloze contexts where the information source is overtly external, while only its perceived reliability is manipulated (High-Trust vs. Low-Trust). In a human production experiment, native speakers of Turkish show a robust trust effect: High-Trust contexts yield relatively more -DI, whereas Low-Trust contexts yield relatively more -mIs, with the pattern remaining stable acro
case_studies.summary: The problem of understanding how source trustworthiness affects Turkish evidential morphology is addressed through a study that investigates the past-domain contrast between -DI and -mIs. The AI approach involves using large language models (LLMs) to track this sensitivity in controlled cloze contexts. The outcome shows a robust trust effect, where native speakers of Turkish prefer -DI in High-Trust contexts and -mIs in Low-Trust contexts, with LLMs also demonstrating this sensitivity.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this study's findings, AI practitioners can utilize LLMs to analyze and generate text that takes into account the trustworthiness of the source, leading to more accurate and nuanced language understanding. Furthermore, practitioners can design experiments to investigate the impact of source trustworthiness on language use in various contexts and languages.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this study is the development of language processing tools that can detect and adapt to the trustworthiness of sources, enabling more effective and reliable language-based applications such as fact-checking and sentiment analysis. This technology can be integrated into various products, including chatbots, virtual assistants, and content moderation platforms, to enhance their performance and credibility.

case_studies.title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
case_studies.abstract: As human-AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction are needed. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory. The PCS captures an agent's perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support. Both scales were adapted
case_studies.summary: The problem of measuring successful cooperation in human-AI teamwork is addressed through the development of two scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale. The AI approach uses joint activity theory and evolutionary cooperation theory to ground these scales, which capture an agent's perceived cooperative capability and the emergent sense of teaming. The outcome is the introduction of two theoretically grounded scales for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this research by using the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale to evaluate the effectiveness of human-AI teamwork in their own projects. By doing so, they can identify areas for improvement and develop more effective human-AI collaboration strategies.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of these scales could lead to the creation of a product or service that helps organizations evaluate and improve their human-AI teamwork, potentially leading to increased productivity and efficiency. A company could be founded to offer consulting services or software solutions based on these scales, providing a concrete business opportunity.
